title: Cricket for Beginners: How the Game Works
summary: Cricket has two teams, a ball, and a bat. Teams score runs and try to get batters out.

cover.alt: A batter faces a bowler on a sunny cricket pitch while a wicketkeeper and fielders watch.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Cricket has two teams, a ball, and a bat. Teams score runs and try to get batters out.

items.prompt: What sports use a bat and a ball?
Do you know a country where cricket is popular?

blocks.title: Part 1: Teams, Pitch, and Wickets
paragraphs: This simple guide explains cricket for beginners.
A cricket match has two teams. Each team has eleven players. One team bats. The other team fields.
The main action happens on the pitch. It is a long area in the centre. There is one wicket at each end of the pitch.
A wicket has three wooden sticks. These sticks are called stumps. Two small wooden pieces sit on top. They are called bails. The wickets are important targets in the game.

images.alt: Two batters stand at opposite ends of a long cricket pitch as a bowler, wicketkeeper, and fielders take their positions around two wickets.

blocks.title: Check: Part 1: Teams, Pitch, and Wickets

items.prompt: How many teams and players are in a standard cricket match?
items.answer: There are two teams, and each team has eleven players.

blocks.title: Part 2: The Players and Their Jobs
paragraphs: The batter uses a bat. The batter tries to hit the ball and score runs. Two batters are on the pitch. They stand at opposite ends.
The bowler bowls the ball toward the batter and wicket. The bowler tries to stop runs or get the batter out.
The wicketkeeper stands behind the wicket. This player catches or stops the ball. The other players are fielders. They stand around the field. They catch the ball, stop it, and throw it back.

blocks.title: Check: Part 2: The Players and Their Jobs

items.answer: The wicketkeeper stands behind the wicket and catches or stops the ball.

blocks.title: Part 3: Runs, Fours, and Sixes
paragraphs: Runs are the points in cricket. For one run, the two batters run and safely change ends.

A batter can also score a boundary. The edge of the field is the boundary. A ball that reaches it after touching the ground scores four runs. A ball that goes over it without touching the ground scores six runs.
Here is an example. Team Blue scores one run, then four, then six. The total is eleven. The scoreboard can show “Team Blue 11/0.” This means eleven runs and no batters out.

images.alt: Three cricket scenes show batters changing ends, a ball rolling to the boundary rope, and a ball flying over the rope.

blocks.title: Check: Part 3: Runs, Fours, and Sixes

items.prompt: Team Blue has 11 runs and then scores a four. What is the new score?
items.explanation: Would you prefer to run for one run or try to hit a boundary? Why?

blocks.title: Part 4: Six Balls in an Over
paragraphs: The bowler does not bowl forever. Cricket divides the bowling into short groups. One group is called an over.

An over has six valid balls. A valid ball is a delivery that counts in the game. The bowler bowls the first valid ball. Then the second ball counts. This continues until the sixth valid ball. The over is then complete.
Overs help players count the game. For example, three complete overs contain eighteen valid balls.

blocks.title: Check: Part 4: Six Balls in an Over

items.prompt: How many valid balls are in two complete overs?
items.answer: Two complete overs contain twelve valid balls.

blocks.title: Part 5: Three Ways to Get a Batter Out
paragraphs: When a batter is out, that batter’s turn ends. Another batter usually comes to the pitch.
There are several ways to get a batter out. Here are three common ways.
Bowled: The bowler’s ball hits and breaks the wicket.
Caught: The batter hits the ball. A fielder catches it before it touches the ground.
Run out: A batter is outside the safe area near the wicket. A fielder uses the ball to break that wicket fairly.

blocks.title: Check: Part 5: Three Ways to Get a Batter Out

items.prompt: A fielder catches the batter’s hit before the ball touches the ground. How is the batter out?

blocks.title: Part 6: Test, ODI, and T20 Cricket
paragraphs: Cricket has three main international formats. An innings is one team’s turn to bat.
A Test match can last five days. Each team can have two innings. Test cricket is the longest format.
An ODI is a One Day International. Each team has 50 overs.
A T20 International has 20 overs for each team. It usually takes about three hours. It is the shortest of these three formats.
The basic ideas stay the same. Teams bat, bowl, field, score runs, and get batters out.

images.alt: Three cricket matches move from repeated days to one day and then a short floodlit evening game.

blocks.title: Check: Part 6: Test, ODI, and T20 Cricket

items.prompt: Which format has 20 overs for each team?
items.answer: A T20 International has 20 overs for each team.
